handback.title: One shared Dokima App with a one-click install
handback.summary: Every repo runs Dokima through one shared App, set up fully by its install.
handback.feature: Installing one shared App onboards a repo fully; runs get tokens from a small service, and self-made Apps still work.

stories.title: Register the shared App from a prefilled manifest
stories.user_story: The owner registers Dokima's shared App with one click, and never handles its private key.

acceptance_criteria.text: The shared App's manifest asks for write access to workflows, secrets and administration.
acceptance_criteria.words: The cost is broader App permissions (workflows, secrets, administration)
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the owner runs registration, GitHub's new App page opens prefilled, so one Create click registers it.
acceptance_criteria.words: a prefilled App manifest, so the owner clicks Create once
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the owner clicks Create, the App's private key is stored in the service and never saved to disk.
acceptance_criteria.words: GitHub hands the App's private key straight to the setup script, which stores it in the service. No download, and no customer ever holds it.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

stories.title: A small service trades a run's identity for a token
stories.user_story: Runs on any repo act as Dokima's shared bot, while its private key stays in one place.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a run sends its signed identity, the service returns a short-lived token for that repo only.
acceptance_criteria.words: exchanges it with a small service dokima-dev hosts, which checks the run really is that repo with Dokima installed and returns a short-lived token scoped to it
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the run's repo does not have the shared App installed, the service refuses and returns no token.
acceptance_criteria.words: checks the run really is that repo with Dokima installed
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the signed identity is forged, expired or for another repo, the service refuses and returns no token.
acceptance_criteria.words: checks the run really is that repo
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a shared App run files a Dokima bug upstream, the service returns a key for that repo.
acceptance_criteria.words: Under the shared App, the service must mint that key instead.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

non_functional.text: The App's private key is read only inside the service, and no reply ever carries it.
non_functional.why: Anyone holding it could act as Dokima everywhere.
non_functional.words: The App's private key never leaves the service.
non_functional.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

stories.title: Runs get their GitHub token from the service
stories.user_story: An adopter's runs act as Dokima's shared bot with no App key stored in their repo.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a repo holds no App key of its own, each run gets its GitHub token from the service.
acceptance_criteria.words: the adopter's workflow requests GitHub's signed identity token (OIDC) and exchanges it with a small service dokima-dev hosts
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a repo holds its own App key, runs act as that self-made App, as they do today.
acceptance_criteria.words: keeping self-made Apps as a fallback for teams that refuse a shared one
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: (manual) A fresh repo on the shared App takes a first issue from autopilot start to merged; needs real GitHub.
acceptance_criteria.words: acceptance item 13 on #272 passes under the shared App, and the self-made App path still works
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

stories.title: Installing the App onboards the repo
stories.user_story: Installing the App sets up each picked repo fully, with no manual step left for the owner.

acceptance_criteria.text: Installing the App puts the Dokima workflow and settings file on the default branch, with no pull request.
acceptance_criteria.words: Installing the App onboards everything with no setup PR. Our service adds the workflow and `settings.yaml`
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When onboarding finishes, a first issue is open on the repo.
acceptance_criteria.words: and opens a first issue
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the repo's default branch is not main, onboarding writes to that branch.
acceptance_criteria.words: **Default branch** read from the repo, never assumed to be `main` (#874).
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When onboarding finishes, the repo holds a code owners file naming the owner who installed the App.
acceptance_criteria.words: **CODEOWNERS** naming the owner who may give commands and approve.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When onboarding finishes, the repo variable holds the App's id.
acceptance_criteria.words: **App id** set as the repo variable.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When onboarding finishes, every label Dokima uses exists on the repo, and labels already there are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.words: **Labels** Dokima uses created up front
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the repo has a tests folder, onboarding names it in the settings, so test runs stay inside it.
acceptance_criteria.words: **Tests folder** found or asked for, and Dokima's test runs scoped to it (#877).
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the repo has no tests yet, onboarding still finishes and the first issue asks where tests will live.
acceptance_criteria.words: Handle a repo with no tests yet without failing the baseline.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

stories.title: Onboarding protects the default branch
stories.user_story: Nothing merges unproven on an onboarded repo, while the owner can still push an emergency fix.

acceptance_criteria.text: When onboarding finishes, the default branch requires the all tests and Acceptance criteria checks.
acceptance_criteria.words: **Required checks always on** (`all tests`, `Acceptance criteria`): nothing merges unproven
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When onboarding finishes, the default branch requires a code owner's approval.
acceptance_criteria.words: **Owner (code-owner) approval on by default**
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When onboarding finishes, the rules do not bind admins, so the owner can push directly.
acceptance_criteria.words: **Admin enforcement off**, so the owner can still push an emergency fix.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: On a free private repo, onboarding finishes without protection and says what is lost and how to get it.
acceptance_criteria.words: Setup must detect that and say so plainly (what is lost, how to get it), not fail.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

stories.title: The setup page after install
stories.user_story: After installing, the owner adds their model key on GitHub and chooses whether Dokima's bugs reach its team.

acceptance_criteria.text: After install, the setup page links straight to the repo's secrets page on GitHub.
acceptance_criteria.words: After Install, the setup page links the customer straight to their repo's GitHub secrets page, and they paste the key there.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the owner ticks the bug report box, the repo's upstream setting names Dokima's repo.
acceptance_criteria.words: The setup page has a checkbox, "Send Dokima's own bugs to the Dokima team". It writes the upstream-repo setting from #745
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the owner leaves the bug report box unticked, the upstream setting stays off.
acceptance_criteria.words: which stays off by default
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

non_functional.text: The setup page has no field for the model key, and the service never receives one.
non_functional.why: The key stays with the owner and GitHub.
non_functional.words: The model key never touches Dokima's service.
non_functional.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

stories.title: Bug reports filed home under the shared App
stories.user_story: Dokima's own bugs reach its team from any repo, carrying nothing of the repo's own code.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a run on the shared App files a Dokima bug upstream, the issue opens using the service's key.
acceptance_criteria.words: Under the shared App, the service must mint that key instead.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a raise is filed upstream, it carries only Dokima's step, its error and the version, no code blocks.
acceptance_criteria.words: Recommended: send only Dokima's step, its error from Dokima's own code and the version; drop code blocks and non-Dokima paths.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

stories.title: Onboard a repo from the command line
stories.user_story: An owner with the GitHub command line onboards another repo with one command.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the owner runs the init command on a repo, it joins the existing install and gets onboarded.
acceptance_criteria.words: Adds the repo to the existing installation
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the init command is given the model key, it is stored as a repo secret, not in an environment.
acceptance_criteria.words: App key and model key placed where the thin install can read them: repo secrets, not the `keys` environment (#876).
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Its own planner lists them with its tests.

raises.label: App already registered
raises.text: The App is already registered. Is the prefilled manifest still wanted? The plan keeps it, to set its permissions.
raises.evidence: The 2026-10-18 comment names App ID 5373929, already registered as dokima-dev.

raises.label: Setup as pull request
raises.text: Should teams refusing the broad permissions get the setup as a pull request instead? The plan leaves this out.
raises.evidence: The 2026-10-18 comment marks it Open: offer review as a PR instead.

raises.label: What bug reports carry
raises.text: Should bug reports filed home carry only Dokima's step, its error and the version? The plan assumes so.
raises.evidence: The 2026-10-18 comment leaves this open for Reza, with that recommendation.
